parsed.summary: Two statements are formalized. `standardQuantumParallelRepetition` says that every finite game with entangled value below 1 has repeated entangled values bounded by C·exp(−c n) for some c, C > 0. This is a faithful qualitative form of the quantum parallel repetition result. `distributionUniformExponential` is meant to be the quantitative Theorem 1.1, but it only requires the universal constant to satisfy c ≥ 0. With c = 0 the bound reads ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ 1, which is trivial, so the quantitative theorem is effectively not formalized.

glossary.plain: Finite two-player one-round game: a probability weight µ(x,y) on X×Y and a Boolean predicate V(x,y,a,b).
n-fold parallel repetition: product question distribution; the players win iff every coordinate is won.
Family of PSD effects summing to the identity.
Finite-dimensional tensor-product strategy: a shared state on Alice⊗Bob, plus a POVM per question for each player.
glossary.note: Dimensions are finite but arbitrary; the sup over these is the standard ω*.

glossary.plain: Σ_{x,y} µ(x,y) Σ_{a,b} V(x,y,a,b)·Re tr(ρ (A^x_a ⊗ B^y_b)).
sSup of winning probabilities over all finite-dimensional strategies.
glossary.note: If A or B is empty there are no strategies and the value is the junk value sSup ∅ = 0.
The extra constant C is harmless up to adjusting constants.

lean_claims.plain: There exists c ≥ 0 such that for every finite game G with A and B nonempty and ε = 1 − ω*(G) > 0, and every n ≥ 1: ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c·ε^13/(ε + log(|A||B|))·n).
For every finite game G, if ω*(G) < 1 then there exist c > 0 and C > 0 with ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ C e^{−cn} for all n ∈ ℕ.

paper_claims.plain: There exists a universal c_qs > 0 such that for every finite game G with nonempty answer alphabets and ε = 1 − ω*(G) > 0, ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_qs ε^13/(ε + log(|A||B|)) n) for all n ≥ 1.
For every finite game G with ω*(G) < 1 there is c_G > 0 with ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_G n) for all n ≥ 1.

coverage.why: The constant is only required to be ≥ 0, so c = 0 gives the trivial bound ω* ≤ 1.
Uses a C·e^{−cn} bound, which is equivalent to an e^{−c'n} bound for n ≥ 1 after adjusting constants (given values < 1).

flags.explanation: The statement asks for ∃ c, 0 ≤ c rather than 0 < c. Taking c = 0, the right-hand side is exp(0) = 1. Every winning probability is ≤ 1, and sSup ∅ = 0, so ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ 1 always holds. The quantitative theorem therefore becomes vacuous.
flags.probe_idea: Prove distributionUniformExponential by `refine ⟨0, le_rfl, ?_⟩` followed by showing entangledValue ≤ 1 (simp; Real.exp_zero).

flags.explanation: With an empty answer set no POVM or strategy exists, so ω* = sSup ∅ = 0. This only affects degenerate games; Theorem 1.1 assumes Nonempty, and in standardQuantumParallelRepetition the empty case is trivially true.
flags.probe_idea: Prove BddAbove (Set.range winProbability), and that the range is Nonempty when A and B are nonempty.

lint_verdicts.why: Win probabilities are bounded by 1, and the range is nonempty when the answer sets are nonempty; the empty case only matters degenerately.
The denominator is ε + log(|A||B|) ≥ ε > 0 under the hypotheses.
The argument |A||B| ≥ 1 because Nonempty A and Nonempty B are assumed.
